name: African Socialism
summary: African socialism holds that traditional African communities were already communal and classless, so socialism is an indigenous inheritance to be restored rather than an import from Europe. It favours a large public sector guiding development, state or cooperative ownership of land and major industry, self-reliance over foreign aid and capital, Africanisation, non-alignment and Pan-African unity. It rejects class struggle as a European idea and stresses work, communal obligation and leaders who live as they preach, while practice ranged from Tanzania's village collectivisation to Senegal's mixed economy.
scope: The mainstream of the family as it was at its peak in the 1960s-70s, centred on Julius Nyerere's Ujamaa and the Arusha Declaration (1967), with Senghor's Senegal and Nkrumah's Ghana as variants described in the reference sources. Senghor's moderate, France-linked model and Nkrumah's more Marxist-leaning one answered some statements differently. Later Marxist-Leninist African regimes are excluded. Source texts are reached through the Arusha Declaration, a German translation of Nyerere's 1962 Ujamaa essay, and two Wikipedia articles, so Senghor and Nkrumah are covered only second-hand.

keyFigures.name: Julius Nyerere
keyFigures.role: Tanzania's first president and author of Ujamaa and the Arusha Declaration.

keyFigures.name: Léopold Sédar Senghor
keyFigures.role: Senegal's first president, who linked a moderate socialism to Négritude.

keyFigures.name: Kwame Nkrumah
keyFigures.role: Ghana's first leader, who expanded state control and promoted Pan-African socialism.

sources.usedFor: Villagization, nationalization, one-party context, gender, outcomes.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Arusha-era policy put social services under the state for the peasants and workers, and Tanzania's Ujamaa years are credited with falling infant mortality and rising life expectancy.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Not directly addressed; inferred from the Arusha concern that incomes from different work not be grossly divergent and that no one exploit wage earners.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Nyerere rejects capitalism as a system built on exploiting people, and the Arusha Declaration puts the main means of production under state or cooperative control.

public-ownership.rationale: The Arusha Declaration places banks, trade, heavy industry, minerals and land under the state on behalf of peasants and workers; Nkrumah's Ghana likewise expanded state shares in key sectors.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: The state is to prevent wealth accumulation that conflicts with a classless society, though the sources stress leadership codes and ownership over tax rates.

unions-good.rationale: Workers are named as a ruling constituency of the party, but ruling parties in this tradition also tied unions to the state; inferred from the worker-and-peasant orientation.

property-fundamental.rationale: Wealth is held in trust for the community, not as personal property, and unconditional freehold land is rejected as a foreign import.

regulate-corporations.rationale: African socialism seeks to curb private and foreign capital, through state ownership and limits on private enterprise; Arusha allows foreign investment only in limited form.

cut-welfare.rationale: Ujamaa treats mutual care as the heart of the extended-family community, so cutting welfare as dependency-creating contradicts it, though idle able-bodied people are condemned.

worker-ownership.rationale: Ownership is meant to rest with the nation, peasants through their government and cooperatives, not with workers of each firm; cooperatives are endorsed but the state dominates.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Not addressed; adherent regimes used preventive detention and state security, yet Arusha also affirms rights within the law, so no clear typical answer.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from Arusha's moral emphasis on work and shame of drunkenness and idleness.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Not addressed; no documented position, and ruling parties both stressed national unity over tribal division and guaranteed free expression within the law.

strong-leader.rationale: Adherent states were often dominated by a founding leader (Nkrumah, Nyerere), but Arusha insists on democracy and a leadership code; adherents are split.

state-harmful.rationale: African socialism assigns the state a large role in guiding the economy and social development.

limit-guns.rationale: Not addressed by the ideology; no stated position.

empower-police-military.rationale: Not addressed directly; Arusha calls on citizens to defend the nation against stooges of external enemies but gives no case for larger forces.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the Arusha stress on work as the basis of membership and the dignity of labour.

decide-locally.rationale: Arusha builds self-reliance up from villages and ten-house cells, yet adherent states were centralised one-party states, so adherents split between local and national.

rehabilitation.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the communal, family-centred ethic of brotherhood extended to all people.

traditional-family.rationale: Ujamaa derives from the extended family as the model of society, and its programme promoted the nuclear family, though it is about community more than family law.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Not addressed; mid-century adherents and successor ruling parties were socially conservative and the ideology draws on traditional communal norms.

abortion-legal.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from traditional-community values and the socially conservative stance of adherent governments.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: The movement grew from anti-colonial struggle and Africanisation of business and the civil service to correct colonial inequality.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Not addressed; the creed affirms equal opportunity for women and men, but practice reinforced traditional roles.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Emphasis on African identity and building on pre-colonial traditions is central; Senghor tied socialism to Négritude and Nyerere to the traditional community.

gradual-change.rationale: Nyerere stressed a peaceful path and education, yet Arusha demanded sweeping nationalisation and later villagisation; adherents are split.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Not addressed; Pan-African solidarity extends brotherhood across Africa, suggesting hostility to restriction among Africans.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Arusha commits TANU to work for world peace through the United Nations, but also wariness of Western-controlled economic institutions.

free-trade.rationale: Nyerere was wary of Western-dominated international economic institutions, and the creed stresses economic self-sufficiency over integration into world trade.

nation-first.rationale: Self-reliance and independence are central, but so are Pan-African unity and world peace, so adherents do not simply put the nation ahead of cooperation.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Not addressed; Arusha backs liberation movements and the UN but distrusts outside powers.

open-borders.rationale: Brotherhood is extended from tribe to nation to all Africa and eventually humanity, but no source calls for open borders.

limit-growth.rationale: Development is a core aim and growth was prized as the route out of poverty; inferred, not directly stated.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Anachronistic to the founding texts; no stated position.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Arusha wants modern tools and methods in agriculture but puts people, land and hard work above technology and money.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Not addressed by the ideology; no basis for a position.

revolution-justified.rationale: Nyerere rejected class-conflict revolution as unnecessary in Africa, while Nkrumah and Touré backed liberation struggle; contested.

experts-over-public.rationale: Arusha insists government be chosen and led by peasants and workers themselves, but planning by a state bureaucracy was the practice.

central-planning.rationale: A large public sector guiding development, state banks and state direction of the economy are core, though Nyerere warned against top-down development in favour of village-based growth.

socialized-markets.rationale: Adherents differed: Senghor kept much of the market and French ties while Ghana and Tanzania expanded state control; no single answer.

land-value-tax.rationale: Land is to belong to the nation with use rights, not be taxed as private property.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the aim to prevent wealth accumulation against a classless society.

basic-income.rationale: Contradicts the principle that everyone able must work and that idleness is shameful, yet the ideology stresses community care.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: State-led industrialisation and economic self-reliance in Ghana and Tanzania implied protection of domestic production against foreign competition.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Nkrumah's Ghana expanded state industry and the Arusha Declaration put the major means of production under state control, which implies state-directed investment; the cited Wikipedia passage is a summary, not a source statement.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Peasant smallholdings persisted, but Ujamaa aimed at communal village ownership of land and the nation, not small owners as an ideal.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: The Declaration speaks of incomes from different work not grossly divergent, accepting wages and money; abolition is a Marxist, not African socialist, aim.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Banks were nationalised after Arusha and state banks favoured; central banks are strongly state-run.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Not documented as a position; the ruling party and state mediated between groups but without formal corporatist bodies.

one-party-rule.rationale: Many adherent states became one-party states, and Arusha defines TANU as the party of peasants and workers with membership by commitment, though it also insists on democracy.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Not addressed; independence-era movements abolished or bypassed colonial-era chiefs and monarchies in favour of republics.

democracy-best.rationale: Arusha holds that true socialism cannot exist without democracy and Nyerere says democracy has roots in traditional society.

direct-votes.rationale: Traditional consensus discussion is praised, but no source supports direct popular votes on laws.

workers-councils.rationale: Political power was meant to run through the party, parliament and cooperatives, not workers' councils.

right-to-secede.rationale: Independence leaders accepted inherited colonial borders and pursued national unity; Pan-African unions sought merger rather than splitting.

natural-rulers.rationale: Traditional society had no castes or classes and all people are equal; leaders were to be peasants or workers.

political-violence-never.rationale: Nyerere stressed peaceful methods, but Nkrumah, Touré and Cabral supported armed liberation struggle; contested.

war-builds-character.rationale: Arusha commits to world peace through the UN; no glorification of war is documented.

separate-church-state.rationale: Arusha guarantees freedom of religion and equal treatment regardless of religion, but says nothing on strict separation; Senghor was Catholic and Nkrumah drew on Christian and Islamic traditions.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Law was to rest on a secular ideology of socialism and equality, with religion a matter of personal belief.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Arusha puts the major means of production and public institutions under the people's control through the state, which clearly rules out private courts and defence, though the sources do not discuss them.

military-superiority.rationale: Resources were directed to development and self-reliance; no pursuit of military superiority is documented.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Nyerere's brotherhood extends beyond tribe and nation, and the creed bars unequal treatment by race or religion.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Nyerere explicitly rejects class struggle as a European philosophy of conflict and Senghor likewise rules it out.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Arusha demands equality and income differences not grossly divergent, though framed around dignity and fair shares for those who work.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Land belongs to the community; extending this to indigenous peoples within African states is not discussed and the ideology treats all Africans as indigenous.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Colonial rule is seen as having imposed economic dependence, but reparations are not a documented demand.

civilizational-union.rationale: Pan-Africanism was a shared goal and Nkrumah led efforts at union such as with Mali and Guinea, though this is continental rather than religious.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Socialism as attitude of mind means caring for the family and community; Nyerere condemns accumulating wealth for personal insurance or private gain.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Everyone owes work to the community, and the Arusha creed also guarantees rights to expression, movement and religion within the law.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: None of the founding texts discuss the intrinsic value of nature; their concern is land use by the community, so adherents have no settled view.

limit-population.rationale: Not addressed; the ideology does not frame poverty as population and emphasises social causes.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Development and modernisation are goals; ujamaa idealised traditional community but aimed at progress, not anti-industrialism.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Wants modern methods but within planned development; no endorsement of disruptive acceleration.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Anachronistic; government is to be led by peasants and workers themselves.

restore-past-order.rationale: Idealises pre-colonial communal society as a foundation, but aims at modern development, not restoration alone.

results-over-ideology.rationale: The Arusha creed is explicitly ideological and requires party members to accept its faith and be trained in it.

direct-action.rationale: Change was pursued through party, parliament and state, not through direct action.

means-match-ends.rationale: Nyerere says socialism is a way of life that must be practised, and leaders must live as they preach.

return-to-foraging.rationale: African socialism aimed at rural development and modern production; hunter-gatherer life was never proposed, so rejection is inferred.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Not a stated aim; African socialism accepts differentiated work in a classless society.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Distribution by contribution is emphasised (those who sow share in the harvest), though family care of the needy is valued.

production-for-use.rationale: Socialism is defined against exploitation and capitalist profit; production serves the community's people.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Nyerere rejects capitalism as built on exploiting people, though not by Marx's theory of surplus value.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Nyerere rejected Marxist class-conflict theory and a classless society was held to exist or be restorable without it.

collective-farming.rationale: Ujamaa villages with communal farms were the core rural policy, though forced collectivisation of family farms became a major grievance.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Not a documented position, though anti-imperialism is strong; Nkrumah's neo-colonialism critique is related but not cited here.

taxation-theft.rationale: The state funds social services and development; the ideology treats wealth as held in trust for the community.

harm-principle.rationale: The founding texts never discuss limits on state interference in these terms, and communal duties are stressed over individual liberty, so no position is inferable.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Land, wealth and obligations are communal, and brotherhood outranks individualism.

conscription.rationale: Arusha says citizens must be ready to defend the nation when called upon, but not conscription as such.

exit-over-voice.rationale: African socialism stressed participation and collective duty and never weighed exit against voting; disagreement is inferred.

state-as-business.rationale: Nyerere and Nkrumah treated the state as the organiser of public and community ownership; the customer model of government was never discussed, so rejection is inferred.

positive-liberty.rationale: Arusha ties real independence and dignity to material means such as land, tools and services provided collectively.

media-academia-power.rationale: The sources do not claim that universities and media outweigh elected officials; this is outside the ideology's concerns.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Racial equality and rejection of colonial racial hierarchy are foundational; the creed bars unequal treatment by race.

organic-representation.rationale: Traditional communal consultation is valued, but representation ran through a mass party and parliament.

total-state.rationale: State steers economy and social development, but Arusha affirms freedom of religion and expression within the law and rejects total control.

national-rebirth.rationale: Anti-colonial renewal themes exist, but not decadence rhetoric.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Pan-African union was voluntary; no expansionism, and borders inherited from colonial rule were largely accepted.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Rejects feudalism explicitly: a socialist state is one where neither capitalism nor feudalism exists.

bound-labor.rationale: Rejects feudalism and exploitation; land belongs to the nation with use rights for those who work it.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Not addressed; Négritude and decolonisation themes touch on it but are not core.

universal-morality.rationale: Nyerere's brotherhood of all people reaches ultimately all humanity, and the TANU creed states all humans are equal, though not framed as reason-based universals.

single-common-good.rationale: Politics aims at the community's common welfare; classless unity is assumed rather than balancing class interests.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Not addressed by the ideology; adherent states differed in their relations.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Pan-Africanism has long welcomed diaspora Africans (Ghana under Nkrumah did), but this is not a stated principle in the cited sources.

revive-national-language.rationale: Cultural revival is central and Tanzania built nation and socialism around Swahili, but revival of a fallen-out-of-use language is not documented.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Cooperatives and worker-peasant control of enterprise are endorsed, but control runs through party and state.

school-vouchers.rationale: Education was a state responsibility with public investment, as in Senghor's Senegal and Tanzania.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Not directly addressed; Arusha warns against debt reliance in the form of foreign loans, not domestic deficits.

economic-freedom.rationale: Rejects capitalism and holds that political freedom requires a socialist, not market, economy.

rule-by-example.rationale: The Arusha leadership code is about leaders living by their beliefs and not off another man's sweat, which echoes moral example, though code and law accompany it.

national-self-determination.rationale: Anti-colonial independence is the founding aim of the movement.

force-without-un.rationale: Arusha commits to world peace via the UN and the movement was non-aligned; no stated case for unilateral force.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Nyerere describes socialism as an attitude of mind and Négritude privileged emotion and culture; not a rationalist creed.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Not addressed; Pan-African brotherhood cuts against exclusion, but the national welfare state is for citizens.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Nyerere's Ujamaa insists that every able person must work and that idleness is a disgrace, but welfare-benefit conditionality as such is a modern framing he did not address.

class-collaboration.rationale: Rejects class struggle as unnecessary since traditional society was classless; cooperation inside the community is the ideal.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Cultural heritage and African tradition are the foundation of the ideology.

dominated-front.rationale: Non-alignment and Pan-African solidarity against Western economic domination are core, with Nyerere wary of Western-controlled institutions.

workers-nation.rationale: Not addressed; class internationalism is not a theme but neither is national-only worker organisation.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: The creed asserts equal opportunity for men and women while practice kept traditional roles.

ban-interest.rationale: Neither Arusha nor Nyerere's essay addresses interest on loans; their objection is to dependence on foreign loans, not to interest as such.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: The creed bars unequal treatment by race and the movement opposed colonial racial hierarchies.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Nyerere denies classes in traditional society and holds the state, led by peasants and workers, as the people's instrument.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Energy policy is outside the founding texts, and no source ties the ideology to fossil fuel expansion or restriction.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Not addressed; Senghor rejected French assimilation of Africans, which suggests opposition to forced assimilation.

elite-replacement.rationale: The great-replacement conspiracy theory is absent from Nyerere, Nkrumah and Senghor; rejection is inferred from their anti-racist, pan-African outlook.

proportional-representation.rationale: Electoral systems are not discussed in the cited sources, and adherent states mostly ran single-party or majoritarian arrangements.

national-mission.rationale: Nkrumah hoped Ghana would advocate socialism across the continent, but missionary export is not a general theme and Nyerere stressed self-reliance.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Not an African socialist analysis; accounts note women's political representation was largely symbolic.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Arusha's leadership code was written to prevent leaders forming privileged exploiting groups, implying a danger of corrupt elites.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: African socialist writers never addressed eugenics; rejection is inferred from Nyerere's stress on the equal dignity of every person.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The ideology assigns the state a broad economic and social role.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: The creed rejects racial discrimination and holds all people equal.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The TANU creed states that all humans are equal and have a right to dignity.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Nyerere built socialism within Tanzania alone through self-reliance, and Nkrumah sought continental unity rather than world revolution.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Anti-colonialism is central, though the specific claim is not documented in the sources.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Religious personal law is not discussed in the cited texts; Arusha only demands equal treatment regardless of religion.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Freedom of religious belief is a stated right in the Arusha Declaration.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: No African socialist text mentions a cattle-slaughter ban, and the pastoral and farming economies they planned for slaughter cattle; mild disagreement is inferred.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Not addressed; Arusha guarantees religious freedom but not a school policy.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Arusha warns of internal stooges for external enemies, but withering of the state is not a theme.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Arusha requires government chosen and led by peasants and workers and holds socialism requires democracy.

trade-surplus.rationale: Arusha wants export earnings from agriculture to avoid loans but does not set a mercantilist aim.

population-transfer.rationale: Contrary to the creed of equality and brotherhood across tribe and nation.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Taxation and state ownership are legitimate, so the absolute principle is rejected.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Nyerere rejects the capitalist and conflict-based worldview in favour of cooperation and brotherhood.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: One-party practice excluded rivals, but democratic militancy as such is not addressed.

separated-powers.rationale: Adherent states often concentrated power in the party, though a parliament was retained; no clear stated position.

vanguard-party.rationale: TANU is a party of ideologically committed members, but Nyerere denied that the workers need a revolutionary vanguard in a society without class conflict.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Development was to begin in the villages for the rural majority, and wealth is for the community's benefit.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Leaders are barred from owning rental houses and land belongs to the nation; private housing wealth is discouraged.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Not addressed; adherent states often controlled labour unions.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Poverty is attributed to colonial structures and exploitation, not population.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: The movement sought unity across tribes and nations and built national identity from diverse peoples.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Ujamaa and Nkrumah's Ghana chose leaders through party and elections; selection by lot was never discussed, so rejection is inferred.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Adherent states used preventive detention yet Arusha affirms rights within the law; adherents are split.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Not addressed directly; state control of trade and Senghor's peanut price protection suggest support.

party-controls-media.rationale: Not documented; Arusha lists freedom of expression within the law while one-party states controlled the media.

party-commands-army.rationale: Arusha speaks of defence by citizens but not of who commands the army, so no position is documented.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Citizenship rules are not addressed in the cited sources, and Pan-African brotherhood pulls both ways.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: The leadership code bars second salaries, shares and rent income, and the creed wants incomes not grossly divergent.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Members must accept the party's faith, objects and rules and receive ideological training.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Pan-African unions were advocated but the EU is not specifically addressed.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Constitutional command of the armed forces is not discussed in the founding texts.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Church governance is irrelevant to the ideology, which only guarantees freedom of religious belief.

clerical-rule.rationale: Authority rests with peasants and workers through party and state, not clergy.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Adherent states built national self-reliance and defence, not revolutionary defeatism.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Not addressed; Arusha affirms freedom of expression within the law.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Founding presidents often stayed long in office, but no principle is stated.

recall-officials.rationale: Recall of officials is not mentioned; the leadership code constrains leaders through rules instead.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Non-alignment is a shared goal of African socialism, implying distance from military blocs.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Leaders may not rent out houses, but a general abolition is not stated.

people-in-arms.rationale: Citizens are to be ready to defend the nation, but a standing army remained.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Agriculture and village life are the basis of Ujamaa and traditional community is idealised, though morality claims about cities are only implicit.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Arusha warns town dwellers can exploit peasants, yet the movement relied on educated leaders.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: The defence of African culture against colonial hierarchy implies equal worth of cultures, as in Négritude.

death-penalty.rationale: Capital punishment is not addressed in the cited texts, and adherent states differed in practice.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: School curricula on sexuality are not addressed, though the creed backs equal opportunity for men and women.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Not addressed; unlikely for a state-led modernising education project.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Not addressed in the cited sources; Arusha's moral emphasis on work gives only a weak lean.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Inclusive brotherhood across tribes implies no ethnic descent basis.

minority-language-support.rationale: Tanzania promoted Swahili as the unifying language; minority language support is not documented.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Arusha guarantees freedom of religion but does not say whether religious practice may override general law.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Community obligation and conformity to the common way of life are emphasised.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Arusha holds that loans burden the people and undermine independence, which supports resistance to debt.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Arusha: independence cannot be real if a nation depends on gifts and loans, and political independence must be matched by an economic transformation.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Constitution-making procedure is not described in the cited texts.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Adherent states restricted opposition for development and unity, but Arusha insists true socialism needs democracy.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Arusha rejects reliance on aid, so a duty of rich countries is not the stated focus, though solidarity is accepted.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Not addressed; resources were for development and the UN peace.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: The method of choosing the head of state is not discussed in the cited sources.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Banks were nationalised and the state steers the economy.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Territorial bargaining over a historic homeland is not addressed; adherent states mostly accepted colonial borders.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Wealth is a tool held in trust for the community, and land belongs to the nation.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Not addressed; Nyerere distinguished Ujamaa from Marxism but did not rule on the USSR.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Environmental regulation under uncertainty is outside the founding texts and unaddressed.

collective-defense.rationale: Non-aligned stance against military blocs, yet OAU solidarity; no clear position.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: The sources do not address annexation; self-determination is central but the specific legal claim is not stated.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Religious freedom is guaranteed; curbing church property is not a theme.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Presidents were party leaders in adherent states, such as Nyerere and Nkrumah.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Adherent states maintained inherited borders and national unity.

region-keeps-system.rationale: A region keeping a separate economic system within a larger state is not addressed in the sources.

sacred-ruler.rationale: African socialist writers never discussed sacral kingship; rejection is inferred from their egalitarian, anti-feudal outlook.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Contradicts the aim of limiting wealth gaps.

character-from-environment.rationale: Négritude is about cultural formation and socialism an attitude of mind shaped by community, though not directly stated.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The leadership code binds leaders; government is chosen by the people.

space-expansion.rationale: Anachronistic; development resources go to basic needs.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Not addressed; the ideology aims at popular government without class.

leader-cult.rationale: Nkrumah's Ghana had a prominent leader cult while Nyerere avoided one; split.

equal-parenting.rationale: Family law on custody is not covered by the sources.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Class struggle is rejected, though the leadership code worries about leaders becoming a privileged group.

land-redistribution.rationale: All land belongs to the nation, with use by those who work it; redistribution fits but was by nationalisation not seizure for individual farmers.

refugee-return.rationale: Rights of return for refugees are not addressed in the cited texts.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Colonial borders were largely accepted and ethnic claims opposed as divisive.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Freedom of religious belief is guaranteed.

women-must-cover.rationale: The TANU creed affirms equal rights for all and Nyerere treated religion as a personal choice, which clearly rules out a legal dress mandate for women, though no source discusses it.

common-currency.rationale: Soviet-favoured policy was a national currency, yet Senghor kept the franc zone and Pan-Africanists sought union; split.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Pan-African union across borders was a shared goal, including Nkrumah's attempted union.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Minority cultural self-government is not discussed; the sources stress national unity across tribes.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Diaspora strategy is not discussed in the cited texts, so adherents have no documented answer.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Nyerere explicitly distanced Ujamaa from Marxist theory and grounded socialism in an attitude of mind and tradition.

ban-cartels.rationale: Not addressed; state ownership rather than antitrust was the remedy.

no-bailouts.rationale: Bank and firm rescues are not addressed; state ownership of banks means public money already backs them.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: The role of courts against majorities is not covered in the founding texts.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Equal opportunity in the creed, but quotas are not documented as a principle.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Self-reliance is central, though shutting off outside trade is not a stated aim.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Binding standards in trade agreements are not addressed; Nyerere distrusted outside economic institutions generally.

moral-incentives.rationale: Arusha treats work as something to be proud of and leaders as moral examples, with socialism as an attitude of mind.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Guinea-Bissau's Cabral led armed struggle but this is not an African socialist principle in general.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: The ideology rejects feudalism and ascribed status.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Reviving African identity and Africanising institutions imply teaching history from an African centre.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: The movement arose against colonial rule, which proponents saw as imposing power structures and dependency.

patriotic-education.rationale: Nation-building was central and TANU stressed loyalty and national service.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Africanisation of business and civil service were policy; preferences by race in African states are consistent.

public-money-creation.rationale: State banks and state control of finance fit; not addressed explicitly.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Capitalism is rejected as exploitative but the Marxist collapse thesis is not held.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Anti-colonial and self-reliance policy resists continued dependence, though Senghor kept French ties.

delink-world-market.rationale: Self-reliance favoured less dependence on aid, loans and investment, but not a full break; Senghor kept ties.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: The thesis about workers in rich countries is a Marxist one the sources do not take up.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: The creed bars unequal treatment on grounds of race or religion.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Arusha lists rights within the law but does not discuss entrenching them against majorities.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Independent states mostly kept the inherited borders, so not void; no stated position.

elective-rulers.rationale: Government is to be chosen by the peasants and workers.

minority-veto.rationale: Traditional consensus is admired but no minority veto is stated.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Resistance to rulers is not discussed in the sources, though the leadership code binds leaders.

parliament-supreme.rationale: The relative authority of parliament is not addressed since the movements were republican and party-led.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Animal welfare is not addressed in the sources.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Animal use is not addressed in the sources.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Wealth is held in trust for the community and not for personal gain, so privileged people owe duties.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Everyone is expected to work for the community.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: The sources contain no critique of mass culture of this kind.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: A hegemony theory of class rule is Marxist and the sources deny classes in traditional society, so they do not address it.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Colonial rule imposed economic dependence, and Nyerere distrusted Western-controlled international economic institutions.

native-born-offices.rationale: Africanisation of the civil service is a goal, but native-born restriction is not stated.

party-own-road.rationale: Nyerere insisted Ujamaa was distinct from Marxism, and the movement is founded on an African, indigenous road.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Arusha: independence cannot be real if a nation relies on gifts and loans, and aid must not be the main development strategy.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Africanisation implied African leadership in African states, though not stated for settlers.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: The sources do not discuss constitutional anti-fascism, which is a European concern.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Not addressed; Nkrumah's Ghana leaned to the USSR.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: American history is not addressed; inferred from the movement's condemnation of colonial exploitation.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Colonial-era monuments are inconsistent with anti-colonialism; inferred.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Programmes for boys and men are not addressed in the sources.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Domestic violence is not addressed; the sources only note limited women's influence on family law.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Core claim: socialism and democracy have African roots and Africa needs its own forms, not imported ones.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Armies were subordinated to the party in several adherent states.

paid-care-work.rationale: Arusha praises rural women's labour but proposes no wage.

more-religion-public.rationale: Arusha guarantees freedom of religion and equal treatment regardless of faith; the programme is secular in character, so a larger public religious role is not part of it.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Pan-Africanism, including Nkrumah's union of Ghana, Mali and Guinea, favoured political unity across colonial borders, though the sources do not address a single divided nation.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Nyerere holds that traditional land rights lasted only with use, and says freehold ownership is a foreign concept leading to speculation.

filial-duty.rationale: Nyerere grounds African socialism in the extended family with mutual duties of care across generations.

office-by-exam.rationale: Inferred from the Arusha stress on leaders answerable to the party and people; examinations for office are not discussed.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Arusha-era policy nationalized key industries and stressed self-reliance over foreign capital.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Not addressed; Ujamaa gender policy and customary family views pull in different directions.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Not addressed directly; the Arusha texts stress accountability to the people but within one-party structures.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Inferred from the state-led provision of social services in Arusha policy and rejection of private capital accumulation.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Inferred from state or cooperative budgeting under party and assembly oversight; not stated directly.

single-official-language.rationale: Tanzania made Swahili the national language, but this is inferred from practice and Pan-African unity rather than the cited texts.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Inferred from Nyerere's view of freehold land as foreign and from self-reliance against foreign control.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Not addressed; the ideology rejects class struggle and does not frame inequality through racial group outcomes.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Inferred from the Arusha emphasis on work, modest living and leaders who do not live off others.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Inferred from Pan-African solidarity and Tanzania hosting liberation movements; arming insurgents is not stated in the sources.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Inferred from non-alignment and self-determination stressed in the reference overview.

corporate-influence.rationale: Arusha-era socialism sought to curb private and foreign capital; inferred from that, since lobbying is not discussed.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Self-reliance over foreign aid and capital implies wariness of outside money; inferred, as NGO funding is not addressed.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Not addressed; Ujamaa valued large communal families, but its states did not centre on pronatal incentives.

residents-only-property.rationale: Land was held communally and by the state, so local control is plausible, but residency rules for purchases are not addressed.

job-guarantee.rationale: Inferred from the Arusha stress that everyone must work and that the state directs the economy; no explicit job guarantee is cited.

democratic-peace.rationale: Not addressed; the tradition stressed non-alignment and Pan-African unity, and adherents did not take a clear line on democratic peace.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Inferred from the communal duty central to Ujamaa, which makes obligation to the community and its laws a moral matter.

non-intervention.rationale: Non-alignment and national sovereignty were core to the family, though Pan-African and anti-colonial solidarity qualified the absolute claim.

industrial-unions.rationale: Not addressed; Tanzania ran party-linked unions, and the by-industry versus craft question was not a stated position.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Ujamaa and the Arusha Declaration built a classless national community open to all and rejected ethnic or religious division.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Inferred from Ujamaa's emphasis on the family and community; abolishing legal marriage runs against that.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Not addressed; a one-party state context pushes against, while the stress on leaders accountable to the people pushes toward openness.

local-production.rationale: Inferred from self-reliance and village-based communal production, which favoured local production, though state planning also stressed national industry.

informal-organisation.rationale: The tradition ran through a ruling party and state, with the Arusha Declaration building TANU as the central organisation.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Inferred from anti-colonial sovereignty, which placed national law and independence above external control; not stated directly.

religious-nation.rationale: Arusha stated that the state must be secular and religion a private matter, and the nation was defined across religious and tribal lines.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Non-alignment, self-reliance over foreign aid and Pan-African unity make tribute-style deference to a great power foreign to the ideology.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the Arusha stress on national planning and equality of incomes, which favours pooling over regional retention.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: The Arusha Declaration puts the major means of production under peasants and workers while Nyerere's essay treats personal property from one's own work as legitimate.

defeat-communism.rationale: Inferred from non-alignment: African socialists refused to join either bloc's crusade, though they also rejected Marxist class struggle.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Inferred from the Arusha model of state-run social services and nationalised major industry; Senghor's mixed economy would allow more private roles.

religion-illusion.rationale: The Arusha Declaration guarantees freedom of religion and Nyerere was a believer, so adherents do not treat religion as a fading illusion.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Nyerere presents capitalism as foreign and exploitative and socialism as the restoration of an older communal order, not a stage built on capitalism.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Inferred from the Arusha commitment to equality and to ending exploitation; Ujamaa's gender record is mixed and the sources give no explicit doctrine.

socialized-care.rationale: Not addressed; the traditional extended family already shares care privately while villagization brought some public services, so adherents are split.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Inferred: Tanzania promoted Swahili as a unifying national language, but the sources describe no policy of purging loanwords.

treaties-binding.rationale: Inferred from the stress on national unity over ethnic or tribal particularism, which leaves little room for treaty-based internal nations.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Nyerere grounds socialism in the extended family and village community, and Ujamaa villages were the policy built on it.

majority-settlement.rationale: Inferred from the ideology's emphasis on national unity and equality; promoting settlement into minority regions is not discussed.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: African socialism presents itself as an indigenous third course, rejecting both capitalism and Marxist class struggle, and held to non-alignment.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Nyerere held that land belongs to the community and nation, but the sources do not take up rival peoples' claims; Pan-Africanism and rejection of colonial borders cut both ways.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Not discussed in the sources; African socialist leaders were anti-colonial and anti-racist, so denial is inferred to be rejected.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Not a stated doctrine, but most African socialist governments kept colonial-era criminal laws and Nyerere's Tanzania did so; contested and inferred from practice.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Tanzania ran a one-party state under TANU on the argument that traditional consensus needs no opposition parties, and Ghana and others followed.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: The Arusha Declaration treats religion as a private matter and the state as secular; not directly addressed.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: African socialism arose in opposition to colonial rule and exploitation and stresses self-reliance and Africanisation.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: A religious-law duty is not part of this secular socialism, though resistance to foreign invasion is supported; inferred.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: The Arusha Declaration treats the state as secular and religion as private; removal for not governing by religious law is outside the ideology.

participatory-democracy.rationale: The Arusha Declaration stresses that people must take part in decisions, and Ujamaa village governance was meant to be run by villagers, though in practice party-led.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: African socialism rejects class struggle as a European idea and stresses communal unity; the framing is not theirs, though they oppose racism and sexism; inferred.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Not addressed; communal and traditional values and the leaders' record on such laws suggest disagreement, inferred at low confidence.

assisted-dying.rationale: Not discussed; the communal obligation to care for people suggests disagreement. Inferred from Nyerere's emphasis on communal duty.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Nyerere and Senghor claimed to follow an indigenous path distinct from both capitalism and Marxism, which fits a combining of ideas; inferred.

alienated-labor.rationale: Nyerere rejected European class analysis but honoured work as the basis of dignity; not addressed in these terms, so split.

islam-incompatible.rationale: The Arusha Declaration accepts religious freedom and equality, and the movement was anti-racist; claims of civilizational incompatibility are foreign to it.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: The Arusha Declaration grounds authority in the people and the party, not God, but traditional religion is respected; not addressed directly.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: The state was secular but stressed religious freedom; a ban on religious dress is not in the sources, so mild disagreement is inferred.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Not addressed; the equality focus suggests support for protecting workers, inferred from the Arusha concern that no one exploit wage earners.

social-market-economy.rationale: African socialism favoured state or cooperative control of major industry, rejecting a mainly market model, though Senghor's Senegal ran a mixed economy.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: African socialist states kept armies and stressed national defence and liberation of the continent; abolition is not on the agenda.

rich-first.rationale: The Arusha Declaration says a socialist state has no exploitation and no great gaps between incomes, and Ujamaa stressed equal sharing.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Non-alignment was central to African socialism, and the Arusha Declaration stresses self-reliance over aid from either camp.

dynastic-succession.rationale: African socialism rejects privilege of birth and chiefly-style rule in a one-party republic that presents leaders as servants of the people, and the Arusha leadership code binds leaders against privilege.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Nyerere's stress on cooperatives and public ownership of finance suggests user-owned credit, but the sources do not discuss credit issued at cost; inferred.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Self-reliance over foreign aid and capital is central, and the Arusha Declaration warns against dependence on loans and foreign money.

property-franchise.rationale: The Arusha Declaration makes all adults equal citizens and bars property-based privilege; leaders are barred from holding property for income.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; Nyerere championed women's equality in the village but not an ecological claim of this kind.

reification.rationale: African socialists blamed capitalism for exploitation but did not use this theory; Nkrumah-style Marxists might agree while Nyerere did not.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Nkrumah's wing and Tanzania nationalised the press, reflecting the view that private wealth distorts liberties; Senghor's wing was less sure. Inferred.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: The Arusha Declaration stresses the rule of law and equality before it, but one-party states often ruled by decree; inferred from stated principles.

racial-franchise.rationale: African socialism built on Pan-African unity and equal citizenship of all races within the nation, and Nyerere's Tanzania was non-racial.

online-participation.rationale: The mainstream predates the internet; its village-meeting democracy suggests openness to participation, but this is an anachronism.

open-government-data.rationale: Anachronistic; the leadership code stresses leaders' accountability but the one-party state did not publish records as such.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Nyerere's state was secular and non-sectarian, and unity across religions was a goal; a marriage restriction is inferred as contrary to it.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Ujamaa insists on unity of all people in the nation across tribe and religion, so targeting a minority's shops contradicts it.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Nyerere's Ujamaa idealised traditional village discussion in which elders and members talk until they agree, which is close in spirit to ordinary people deliberating and deciding, though the sources do not mention assemblies by lot (inferred).

reinterpret-religion.rationale: The sources do not address religious doctrine; leaders such as Nyerere were Christian and favoured a secular state without pressing theological reform, so adherents are not clearly for or against it (inferred).

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: The Arusha Declaration condemns exploitation and the leadership code bars leaders from accumulating wealth, reflecting the view that great private wealth undermines equality.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Inferred from the traditionalist, communal social outlook of the 1960s-70s; the sources do not discuss it.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: The Arusha Declaration affirms freedom of worship and a state neutral on religion, and Ujamaa drew on communal tradition, not state atheism.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Inferred from its state-led, order-oriented development model; abolition is not discussed.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Nyerere stressed national unity against tribalism and favoured consensus within one party rather than guaranteed communal shares; inferred.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Inferred from its emphasis on a large public sector and state or cooperative provision rather than charity.

term-limits.rationale: Practice split: Nyerere stood down voluntarily while Nkrumah held power long-term; not stated in the sources.

vote-delegation.rationale: Inferred from its preference for communal consensus and party-based participation over individual delegation; anachronistic.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from its focus on present self-reliance and development needs.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Inferred from Arusha's commitment to equality of all citizens regardless of sex; religious office is not discussed.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Inferred from Arusha's equality principle and Ujamaa's stress on women's work; practice was uneven.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the citizen-based national and Pan-African outlook of the Arusha era.

rent-control.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from Arusha-era state ownership of major means of production and a state that took over rented housing in the same period.

abolish-ip.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the emphasis on self-reliance and collective ownership, which does not favour private monopolies on knowledge, though this was not a stated policy.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; inferred from the TANU Youth League, Ghana's Young Pioneers and national service schemes of the era, which drilled youth for nation-building.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from non-alignment and the Pan-African push for an Africa free of foreign weapons.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Non-alignment and self-reliance against foreign capital and aid are stated principles, which make foreign bases a threat to independence.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the anti-colonial outlook, which would favour official acknowledgement of colonial crimes.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: The Arusha Declaration condemns exploitation and holds that those who live off the work of others are wrong, and Nyerere stresses work for all members of the community.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from a mainstream nationalist view that accepts lethal force in defence of self and country.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Adherents are split: Nyerere claims continuity with traditional communal society, but the new nations were built across many peoples and he stressed forming a modern nation.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from a mainstream outlook that treated sex as a natural fact and gender roles as the cultural matter.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from women's wings in the ruling parties, which treated women as a shared political group.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from a secular state and religious freedom under the Arusha Declaration, which tempered sacred veneration of the national dead.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the Arusha Declaration's secular programme of socialist construction and rejection of class struggle as European.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Inferred from Pan-Africanism, in which Africa is a spiritual and cultural centre for the diaspora, as under Nkrumah's Ghana.

culture-before-state.rationale: Inferred from the state-led development and nation-building of the era, which put the state first.

god-not-male.rationale: Not addressed; the Arusha Declaration treats religion only as a matter of freedom, so views on describing God are not stated.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Not addressed; the Arusha Declaration treats religion only as a matter of freedom, so adherents hold no view on judging religious texts.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Africanisation of the economy is a listed feature of African socialism, favouring economic roles held by indigenous Africans.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Inferred from the commitment to inherited colonial borders and the fight against tribalism, which opposes regions drawn by people.

independent-unions.rationale: Arusha-era Tanzania folded unions into the party-state structure; inferred from the one-party, state-guided model, and Nyerere did value workers' voice.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Ujamaa stresses that socialism is a communal attitude of the people working together; inferred, though rule was by a single party rather than workers' organs.

local-essentials-public.rationale: The Arusha Declaration puts major services and the means of production under public control, so water, health and transport stay public.

second-chamber.rationale: One-party African socialist states mostly ran unicameral assemblies; inferred, not addressed in the sources.

municipal-property.rationale: Ownership is by the nation, cooperatives or the village community under Ujamaa; split between local community and state, inferred from village collectivisation versus state ownership.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Ujamaa villages were coordinated from above by party and state, not by confederal bodies; inferred from Tanzanian practice.

family-wage.rationale: Nyerere's emphasis on communal obligation and the family as the basis of society suggests support for family-supporting pay; inferred, not stated.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: A state-led development programme prioritising health services implies support for faster access; not addressed, inferred.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Not addressed; the ideology's focus was basic health and rural development rather than life extension.

anonymous-payments.rationale: State-guided economies with self-reliance and capital controls would resist untraceable money; anachronistic, inferred.

online-anonymity.rationale: One-party states favoured state oversight of citizens; anachronistic, inferred from the model's party-state structure.

person-over-state.rationale: Nyerere's essay says socialism exists to serve the people and human dignity, but communal duty is also stressed; inferred.

spiritual-nature.rationale: The Arusha Declaration and Ujamaa stress human dignity, work and communal ethics, with religion tolerated and widespread among leaders.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Regional self-government was not a concern; the model was centralising but Senghor and Nkrumah differed, so split.

gm-crops.rationale: Anachronistic; self-reliance in agriculture favours it but suspicion of foreign capital and seed firms cuts against it.

dense-cities.rationale: Nyerere's ideal was village life and rural self-reliance, so urban density was not prized; inferred.

racial-group-interests.rationale: African socialism rejects class struggle and held African unity above divisions, with Pan-Africanism as a core aim, so organising by race against others is out of line.

racial-pride.rationale: Africanisation and the restoration of African dignity against colonial contempt are central, so African pride is legitimate.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Non-alignment and anti-colonial liberation backing were central, but Tanzania did fight Uganda in 1978-79; inferred.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Inferred from Nyerere's use of Swahili to unite Tanzania's many ethnic groups and the OAU's acceptance of colonial borders, with Pan-Africanism as continental rather than linguistic unity.

communal-electorates.rationale: African socialists stressed a classless, undivided community and opposed tribal and sectarian divisions; Tanzania ran national, not communal, politics.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Inferred from Nkrumah's and Nyerere's warnings of neo-colonialism and foreign domination of the new states, an idea central to the self-reliance theme in the Arusha Declaration.

free-public-college.rationale: Inferred from the Arusha-era state provision of social services and education for peasants and workers; free higher education was extended by the state in Tanzania.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Not addressed in the 1960s-70s texts; development priorities and state ownership of industry give no stated view on pollution taxes.

future-generations.rationale: Inferred from the communal view of land as held in common for the community, including later generations, in Nyerere's essay on Ujamaa.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Inferred: African socialism stressed communal obligation and equal work, with women's role in village production, but did not claim distinct values for women.

arms-reduction.rationale: Inferred from non-alignment and Nyerere's stress on peace and self-reliance over arms races; not stated as a disarmament program.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Inferred from non-alignment and anti-colonial opposition to the secret deals of the imperial powers over Africa; not stated as a program.

capital-controls.rationale: The Arusha Declaration called for self-reliance and public control of finance and major means of production against dependence on foreign capital.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Inferred: the ideology aimed at strong post-independence states, though its sources do not discuss armed groups.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Inferred: the emphasis on national unity and defence of the new state leaves no place for a duty to refuse wars.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Inferred: African socialist states favoured workers' organisation but usually kept unions under the party, so collective bargaining was not settled.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Anachronistic; the family favoured state services and cooperatives over tax top-ups in largely rural economies.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Inferred: self-reliance and state-led development priorities do not suit fixed borrowing limits, though Nyerere warned against dependence on loans.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: The Arusha Declaration and the wider family stress self-reliance, anti-neocolonialism and a fairer place for poor states in the world economy.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Inferred: these governments mostly took over and used the inherited state and made it the main tool of development.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Inferred: Ujamaa gave a fixed model of village collectives and public ownership, not open choice of systems.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Anachronistic and unaddressed by the sources, so no clear position can be drawn.

sacred-nation.rationale: Inferred: nation-building and Pan-African unity were central, but the family's emphasis was on community and class rather than the nation as sacred.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Inferred: the stress on equality and state provision of education suggests support for relief, though the sources do not discuss it.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Inferred: the Arusha Declaration criticises the gap between town and country and foreign domination, which resembles the core-periphery claim.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Inferred: Nyerere's stress on the equality and dignity of every person points to a common human nature, though the sources do not discuss redesigning it.

public-service-media.rationale: Inferred: governments in the one-party era kept media under state or party control, which counts against independent public media.

religions-one-truth.rationale: The sources do not address religious truth; Nyerere's Arusha Declaration treats religion as a private matter, so inferred as split.

farm-price-support.rationale: The Arusha Declaration favours cooperatives and state-guided agriculture for the peasants, which fits price support and cooperative credit.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: African socialism stressed non-alignment and anti-colonial peace, so it would not defend nuclear arms; inferred from that stance.

workers-own-party.rationale: TANU and the one-party states presented a single national party of peasants and workers and rejected class conflict, so a separate workers' party was not their approach.

ban-fgm.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; modernising leaders such as Nyerere pushed the state to end harmful customs, so inferred at low confidence.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Nyerere's essay stresses that everyone in the community works and shares in its land, so women's equal land rights fit; inferred from that.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Not addressed beyond promoting Swahili as a national language; adherents have no clear view on regional names.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: With public ownership and state planning at its core, African socialism favours state rules over private suits; inferred from the Arusha model.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Nyerere removed chiefs' political powers in 1963 and the Arusha model rests on party and elected bodies, though Senghor's Senegal kept more traditional ties.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Communal obligation outranks individual claims in Nyerere's thought, so an environmental duty can override liberty; inferred, not directly stated.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Not addressed in the sources, and adherents' views vary; no clear inference from the principles.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Promotion of Swahili as the national language was part of building national unity, so a language duty fits; inferred.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Inferred from Arusha-era Tanzania, where unions were folded into the party-state and worker discipline was stressed, so an open-shop rule was not a theme.

voter-id.rationale: Not addressed; electoral administration is not discussed in the sources, so adherents have no stated view.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Arusha guarantees freedom of religion and equal treatment regardless of faith, so privileging one interpretation in law is inferred as unwelcome.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Nyerere held that democracy has roots in traditional consensus and that a one-party state could be democratic, so competitive elections are not the defining test; inferred.

premarital-sex.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the creed's stress on communal obligation and traditional values, with mixed practice.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Not addressed and anachronistic; inferred from the one-party, state-guided model of Arusha-era Tanzania, which used detention and control to protect unity.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Inferred from the emphasis on public provision, communal care and self-reliance rather than cash substitutes for welfare services.

women-suffrage.rationale: Not stated directly; inferred from the creed's equal opportunity for women and men and the anti-colonial mass franchise of the independence parties.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Not addressed; the leaders were believers and the Arusha text guarantees religious freedom, so religion as a main cause of oppression is inferred as rejected.

race-social-construct.rationale: Inferred from the creed's rejection of racial hierarchy and colonial racial ideology; the sources do not discuss the biology of race.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Arusha commits to equal opportunity for women and men, so equality bodies fit; agencies themselves are not documented in the sources.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Treats land as the common inheritance of the community, held in trust and not owned by whoever claims it first.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Not addressed in the founding texts; inferred from anti-colonial scepticism toward external legal bodies judging African leaders.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from a socialism rooted in communal tradition and secular development goals, not scriptural literalism.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the Arusha Declaration's stress on equality and the participation of all citizens.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from its commitment to state-led socialist development, which it would defend against foreign capital and attack.

indirect-election.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the one-party, council-based structures of Tanzania and similar regimes, where higher bodies were chosen from below.

national-church-status.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from its secular, egalitarian national-unity project that gave no legal privilege to one church.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from its emphasis on a single national identity against tribalism, which resisted ethnic territorial autonomy.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from its stress on self-determination, set against its support for existing borders.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Not addressed in the cited sources; inferred from its nation-building and Pan-African unity aims, which avoided redrawing state boundaries.

simple-living.rationale: The Arusha Declaration stresses self-reliance, hard work, and leaders who live simply, as part of its ideal of society.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from its view of all citizens as members of one nation with equal right to settle anywhere in it.

equal-conscription.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from its stress on national service and duty, set against no stated position on drafting women.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Nyerere holds that land belongs to the community in traditional African life and to the nation, tying people to the ancestral land.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the Arusha stress on leaders' integrity and on communal order, with no stated policy of killing without trial.

close-ties-china.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from non-alignment and self-reliance that favour ties with non-Western partners over reliance on one power.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Not addressed; Pan-African unity is stressed but the sources say nothing of kin minorities across borders.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Nyerere says land is a free gift of God to all, and that no one may own it as a private commodity.

self-ownership.rationale: Not addressed; the ideology stresses communal obligation over individual rights, though not as a denial of rights over the self.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Inferred from Arusha-era policy that gave social services to all peasants and workers, not only the poorest.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Not addressed; the sources describe one-party participation and TANU's role, not bypassing groups.

no-business-privileges.rationale: The Arusha leadership code bars leaders from private business and extra income, so no one gains from a connection to power.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from a national, communal outlook that stands above sectarian divisions.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Nyerere argues for a modern socialist society built on traditional communal values, not a choice between them.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from socialist stress on equality and the emancipation of all workers.

national-resource-control.rationale: The Arusha Declaration puts the major means of production under state control and calls for self-reliance against foreign capital.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Ujamaa and the Arusha Declaration hold that wealth should be shared communally and that exploitation and inequality are wrong, so process alone does not justify a distribution; inferred from those principles.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: The tax is not discussed; inferred from the self-reliance and anti-foreign-capital stance of the Arusha Declaration.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Not addressed directly; African socialists framed the main obstacles as colonial legacy and economic dependence, inferred from the sources' emphasis on those.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Not addressed; adherents were split between natural-law style appeals and state authority, so no clear answer.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Anachronistic; Nyerere stressed that all must work and valued labour, though he favoured development through technology in the long run, so this is split.

multipolar-world.rationale: Non-alignment and Pan-African unity are core aims, rejecting dominance by either bloc.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Nyerere's essay stresses work as the basis of dignity and wealth; the Arusha Declaration says wealth comes from labour, though it is not framed as a formal labour theory of value.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Arusha-era socialism joined nation-building and Pan-African loyalty to serving peasants and workers, and leaders were expected to live as the people do.

material-over-identity.rationale: Anti-colonial identity and African authenticity were central, yet material development of peasants and workers was the stated priority, so adherents combined both.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: African socialism rejected class struggle and Marxist-Leninist vanguard parties as European imports; mixed economies existed (Senegal) but under a single national party, not a communist one.

missingStatements.text: Traditional village communities, not imported ideology, are the proper foundation for a modern socialist society.
missingStatements.rationale: Nyerere's essay bases African socialism on the extended family and traditional community, and the central claim of the ideology is that socialism is indigenous.

missingStatements.text: Land should belong to the community or nation, with people holding it only so long as they use it.
missingStatements.rationale: Nyerere holds that traditional land rights lasted only with use, and says freehold ownership is a foreign concept leading to speculation.

missingStatements.text: Political leaders should be barred from holding company shares, extra salaries or rental property.
missingStatements.rationale: The Arusha leadership code states exactly these bars so leaders do not live off another person's work.

notes: Senghor's Senegal kept the market economy, the French franc and French advisors, and Nkrumah's Ghana leaned toward the Eastern bloc, so adherents split on markets, planning, alignment and leadership; this profile follows Nyerere. Senghor and Nkrumah were not read in their own texts.
